description: Shared foundation that every screen depends on: install deps, expand lib/types.ts to the spec's data model, rewrite data/mock.ts as the Johnson Family (Denver, CO) household, add animation helpers (count-up hook, animated counter, reusable circular gauge, Tailwind keyframes), and apply Vanguard IV + TrustShield branding with smooth page transitions in the shell/sidebar. All later FEATs (002-008) consume this; it must land first.
steps: Run 'npm install' in the project root (node_modules is not present yet), then 'npm run build' to confirm the scaffold is green before changing anything.

Expand lib/types.ts with the new data model (keep existing types that still fit, e.g. Severity). Add: Device { id, name, type (phone|laptop|tv|camera|thermostat|speaker|tablet|console|other), owner, status (online|offline), firmwareOk, lastSeen }; ActivityEvent { id, severityDot (red|amber|green), title, source, timestamp (ISO), relativeLabel }; LiveThreat { id, threatType (phishing|malware|scam|suspicious), source, action (blocked|warned|monitoring), aiExplanation, timestamp }; DeepfakeExample { id, mediaType (video|image|audio), fileName, verdict (likely-ai|authentic|likely-synthetic), confidence, indicators: { label, detail, flagged }[], recommendation }; extend FamilyMember with roleLabel (e.g. 'Dad (Account Owner)'), avatarInitials/avatarColor, and a settings object (safeSearch, socialMonitoring, screenTimeVisible, contentFiltering, appRestrictions all optional booleans), memberAlerts: {id,title,severity,timestamp}[], memberDevices: string[], notifyChannels {push,email,inApp}, notifySeverity; PrivacyMonitorItem { id, label, explanation, kind (analyzed|never-seen) }; AuditLogEntry { id, timestamp, dataAccessed, reason }; DataDashboard { collectedLabel, retentionLabel, sharedLabel }; TrustCategory { id, name, score, note }; ScoreHistoryPoint { month, score }; Recommendation { id, title, detail, pointImpact }. Keep DashboardStat/TrustScoreSnapshot shapes but allow the mock to supply spec values.

Rewrite data/mock.ts entirely as the Johnson Family household in Denver, CO. Export: household meta (name 'Johnson Family', location 'Denver, CO'); 12 devices across the device types; a month (~20-30 entries) of threat history using fake-but-realistic domains (fake-bank-login.com, secure-amaz0n-verify.com, etc.); dashboardStats for the four summary cards (23 Threats Blocked This Week, 156 Devices Scanned, 0 Active Risks, 4 Family Members Protected); recentActivity events matching the spec's five examples verbatim in spirit (phishing blocked / suspicious IoT camera / weekly scan complete / scam call intercepted / new device connected) with red/amber/green dots and relative-time labels; a pool of liveThreats for the real-time feed; 3-4 deepfakeExamples (suspicious video 87% likely AI with inconsistent-lighting + audio-sync + facial-artifact markers; authentic email screenshot; synthetic voice 92% with voice-cloning markers; plus one more); 4 familyMembers (Dad/Account Owner full access, Mom full access, Alex teen 16 with SafeSearch+social monitoring+screen time, Emma child 10 with full parental controls+content filtering+app restrictions) with per-member alerts/devices/settings; privacy monitor items (analyzed: traffic patterns, connection metadata, device fingerprints, DNS queries, behavioral anomalies) and never-seen items (email content, message text, browsing history details, file contents, passwords, personal communications); dataDashboard (2.3 MB anonymized traffic patterns, auto-deleted after 30 days, shared None/on-device); auditLog entries; trustScore overall 87 'Protected' trend up; trustCategories (Network Security 92, Phishing Protection 85, Device Health 88, Privacy Posture 90, Family Safety 80) with the spec notes; scoreHistory 6 months trending up to 87; recommendations with pointImpact values. Add header comment: all data fictional/demo only. Type every export against lib/types.ts.

Add animation helpers: create hooks/useCountUp.ts (a 'use client' hook that animates a number from 0 to a target over a duration, optionally starting when the element enters the viewport via IntersectionObserver, with requestAnimationFrame and cleanup) and components/AnimatedCounter.tsx (client component using useCountUp to render an animating number with an optional suffix). Create components/CircularGauge.tsx (reusable SVG ring gauge: props value 0-100, label, size, optional colored segments for the trust-score screen; may generalize the existing ScoreGauge). Add keyframes/animation to tailwind.config.ts theme.extend (e.g. pulse-slow, fade-in, ping-soft) and any supporting classes to app/globals.css. Keep ScoreGauge working or have CircularGauge supersede it.

Update components/Sidebar.tsx header to show BOTH 'Vanguard IV' and 'TrustShield' branding (TrustShield as product name, Vanguard IV as team), keep the usePathname active-page highlight and the six-item order, and keep it persistent. Add a smooth page-transition wrapper (a fade-in on the content area) in components/AppShell.tsx so navigating between screens animates. Do not break the existing responsive layout.
Run 'npm run build' and fix any type or lint errors introduced by the new types/data/components.
acceptance_criteria: 'npm run build' exits 0 with no TypeScript or ESLint errors.

data/mock.ts exports Johnson Family / Denver, CO data: 4 members (Dad/Mom/Alex 16/Emma 10), 12 devices, a month of threats with fake domains, trust score 87, and the five trust categories with their spec scores.
lib/types.ts compiles and all data/mock.ts exports are typed against it.
components/AnimatedCounter.tsx and components/CircularGauge.tsx exist and build; a useCountUp hook exists.
The sidebar header shows both 'Vanguard IV' and 'TrustShield' and still highlights the active route.
verification: Run 'npm install' (first run) then 'npm run build' from the project root; confirm exit 0 with no errors.
Run 'npm run dev' and load http://localhost:3000/dashboard; confirm it renders without crashing against the new mock data and the sidebar shows both brand names.
findings:
ENVIRONMENT: Node.js was not installed on this Windows machine; installed Node LTS 24.19.0 via `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS`. It is NOT on the current shell PATH, so prefix build commands with: $env:Path = "$env:ProgramFiles\nodejs;$env:Path". Then `npm install` (already run; node_modules present) and `npm run build` both exit 0 with no TS/ESLint errors (all 10 routes compile). The long-running `npm run dev` probe is blocked by the agent harness; use the production build as the verification gate.

lib/types.ts EXPORTS (all additive; existing types kept): Severity; ThreatCategory; ThreatStatus; Threat{id,title,category,severity,status,source,detectedAt,description}; DashboardStat{id,label,value:string,change:number,trend:'up'|'down'|'flat',tone:'safe'|'warning'|'threat'|'accent'}; DeviceType='phone'|'laptop'|'tv'|'camera'|'thermostat'|'speaker'|'tablet'|'console'|'other'; Device{id,name,type:DeviceType,owner,status:'online'|'offline',firmwareOk:boolean,lastSeen}; SeverityDot='red'|'amber'|'green'; ActivityEvent{id,severityDot,title,source,timestamp,relativeLabel}; LiveThreatType='phishing'|'malware'|'scam'|'suspicious'; LiveThreatAction='blocked'|'warned'|'monitoring'; LiveThreat{id,threatType,source,action,aiExplanation,timestamp}; DeepfakeIndicator (legacy); DeepfakeScan (legacy, still used by current checker); DeepfakeVerdict='likely-ai'|'authentic'|'likely-synthetic'; DeepfakeMarker{label,detail,flagged:boolean}; DeepfakeExample{id,mediaType:'video'|'image'|'audio',fileName,verdict:DeepfakeVerdict,confidence,indicators:DeepfakeMarker[],recommendation}; FamilyMemberSettings{safeSearch?,socialMonitoring?,screenTimeVisible?,contentFiltering?,appRestrictions? all optional boolean}; MemberAlert{id,title,severity:Severity,timestamp}; NotifyChannels{push,email,inApp:boolean}; FamilyMember{id,name,role:'guardian'|'teen'|'child',roleLabel,avatarInitials,avatarColor,protectionLevel:Severity,trustScore,devices:number,activeThreats:number,lastActivity,settings:FamilyMemberSettings,memberAlerts:MemberAlert[],memberDevices:string[],notifyChannels:NotifyChannels,notifySeverity:Severity}; PrivacyControl (legacy); DataBroker (legacy); PrivacyMonitorItem{id,label,explanation,kind:'analyzed'|'never-seen'}; AuditLogEntry{id,timestamp,dataAccessed,reason}; DataDashboard{collectedLabel,retentionLabel,sharedLabel}; TrustScoreFactor; TrustScoreSnapshot{overall,grade:'A'..'F',trend,change,factors}; TrustCategory{id,name,score,note}; ScoreHistoryPoint{month,score}; Recommendation{id,title,detail,pointImpact:number}.

data/mock.ts EXPORTS: household={name:'Johnson Family',location:'Denver, CO'} (as const); dashboardStats:DashboardStat[] (23 Threats Blocked This Week / 156 Devices Scanned / 0 Active Risks / 4 Family Members Protected); devices:Device[] (12 items dev-01..dev-12 across all device types); threats:Threat[] (25 entries, Dec 2025-Jan 2026, fake domains like fake-bank-login.com, secure-amaz0n-verify.com); recentActivity:ActivityEvent[] (the five spec events with red/amber/green dots + relativeLabel); liveThreats:LiveThreat[] (8 for the feed); deepfakeScans:DeepfakeScan[] (legacy, 2 kept for current checker); deepfakeExamples:DeepfakeExample[] (4: dfe-01 video 87% likely-ai lighting+audio-sync+facial-artifact; dfe-02 image 96% authentic; dfe-03 audio 92% likely-synthetic voice-cloning; dfe-04 image 89% likely-synthetic); familyMembers:FamilyMember[] (David/Dad guardian 91, Sarah/Mom guardian 89, Alex teen 74, Emma child 82); privacyControls:PrivacyControl[] (legacy); dataBrokers:DataBroker[] (legacy); privacyMonitorItems:PrivacyMonitorItem[] (5 analyzed + 6 never-seen); dataDashboard:DataDashboard (2.3 MB anonymized / 30-day auto-delete / shared None); auditLog:AuditLogEntry[] (5); trustScore:TrustScoreSnapshot (overall 87, grade B, trend up); trustScoreLabel='Protected'; trustCategories:TrustCategory[] (Network Security 92, Phishing Protection 85, Device Health 88, Privacy Posture 90, Family Safety 80); scoreHistory:ScoreHistoryPoint[] (6 months Aug 72 -> Jan 87); recommendations:Recommendation[] (4 with pointImpact).

COMPONENT/HOOK SIGNATURES: hooks/useCountUp.ts -> useCountUp<T extends HTMLElement>({target:number, duration?=1200, decimals?=0, startOnView?=true}) returns {value:number, ref:React.RefObject<T|null>}. Starts on mount when startOnView=false, else when the ref'd element enters viewport via IntersectionObserver; uses requestAnimationFrame with ease-out cubic; renders 0 on first paint (hydration-safe); cleans up on unmount. components/AnimatedCounter.tsx (default export, 'use client') props: {value:number, suffix?, prefix?, decimals?=0, duration?=1200, startOnView?=true, className?}. components/CircularGauge.tsx (default export, server-safe) props: {value:number, label?, size?=180, strokeWidth?=14, segments?:GaugeSegment[], color?, hideCenter?=false, className?} where GaugeSegment={value:number,color:string,label?:string}; single-arc mode uses scoreTone(value) color unless `color` given; segments mode draws stacked colored arcs (for trust-score). components/ScoreGauge.tsx still exists and works. components/PageTransition.tsx ('use client') keys a `.page-transition` fade on usePathname; already wired inside AppShell content area.

TAILWIND (tailwind.config.ts theme.extend) keyframes + animations added: 'fade-in' (animate-fade-in), 'pulse-slow' (animate-pulse-slow), 'ping-soft' (animate-ping-soft). app/globals.css adds a `.page-transition` class (fade-in) plus a prefers-reduced-motion block that disables .page-transition and the three animate-* utilities. Sidebar header now shows 'TrustShield' with 'Team Vanguard IV' subtitle; active-route highlight and six-item nav order unchanged. Palette tokens unchanged: navy/navy-light/navy-lighter, teal(==cyan), emerald, amber, threat. NOTE for later FEATs: legacy exports (deepfakeScans, privacyControls, dataBrokers) and the old DashboardStat-based dashboard are intentionally retained so existing screens keep building; FEAT-002..008 should migrate those screens to the new spec exports and may remove the legacy ones once no screen imports them.
